head: claude/watchdog-close-recurrence
title: WATCHDOG-CLOSE-RECURRENCE: stamp why the reconciler did not close a watchdog-finalised trade [HOLD, Tier 2]
body:
## Summary

Lane **WATCHDOG-CLOSE-RECURRENCE** (Manager Session 2026-10-24). **Tier 2, `landing: hold`. Do not merge without the operator's OK, and do not deploy.**

**Bottom line: the watchdog never closed any of these positions.** `_watchdog_stuck_strategies` sends no order. Its flat branch runs only after the position has read **flat at the venue twice**, and it then finalises the journal row. In all three known `stuck_strategy_watchdog` closes, something else had already closed the position at the venue. Both of those causes are already fixed, and the fixes are **merged and deployed**. This PR adds bookkeeping only: it records **why the forward reconciler had not closed the row first**. That is the one fact that could not be recovered, because the trader journal had already rotated (`journalctl … since=2026-10-15` → `-- No entries --`).

### Evidence (each item marked)

| trade | what closed it at the venue | what was wrong | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6528 bybit_2 XRPUSDT short 56.9 | MEASURED: its own `sl_order_id` `a189d840…` bought 56.9 @ 1.4024 at 2026-10-09T06:40:00.634 (stop 1.40214). Watchdog finalised at 06:42:22. | The broker closed-pnl lookup did not match: it compared against the intended entry, not the venue entry fill. The close was labelled `stuck_strategy_watchdog` and priced off a candle (1.4011). | fixed by #17455; the row now reads `sl` @ 1.4024 |
| 6549 bybit_2 ADAUSDT short 406 | MEASURED: its own `sl_order_id` `e3bf5ffb…` bought 406 @ 0.2477 at 2026-10-10T01:32:08.108 (stop 0.24767). Watchdog finalised at 01:34:33. | Same as 6528. The "exit past stop" was the candle price (0.2489), not the fill. | fixed by #17455; the row now reads `sl` @ 0.2477 |
| 6634 bybit_1 ETHUSDT short 0.44 (pairs_sol_eth_b) | MEASURED: a buy of 0.44 @ 2449.99 at 2026-10-15T17:20:57.644 on order `06f9bde4…`, which is **not** one of its own bracket ids. Its sibling 6622 (trend_donchian_eth_4h, short 19.69) had already been stopped by its **own** SL `0cecf89f…` (buy 19.69 @ 2450.54, 17:16:30.775). At 17:20:58 the monitor still sent 6622's `sl_cross` reduce-only close for 19.69. Bybit clamped it to the 0.44 that was left, which was the pairs leg. | This is a sibling-takeover race on a netted one-way account. | fixed by #18514 (SOAK-MECH-C, merged 2026-10-16, the day after) |

- DECIDED / MEASURED: both fixes are in the running trader. `/api/diag/version` gives `trader_git_sha 4a60daf02`, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms both #17455 (`469983abf`) and #18514 (`005f46075`) are in it.
- MEASURED: how often it recurs (the item's `origin.rerun`, paged through `/api/diag/journal?table=trades&limit=1000&offset=0|1000|2000`, ids 3731..6730):
  - bybit_1, last 200 closed (ids 6301..6712, 2026-09-30..10-23): **1** close is `stuck_strategy_watchdog` (6634).
  - bybit_2, all 89 closed since id 3731 (2026-07-21..10-22): **0**. 6528 and 6549 were relabelled `sl`, with `pre_label_exit_reason` kept.
  - bybit_portfolio, 91 closed: **0**.
  - There has been no watchdog close since 2026-10-15.
- INFERRED, **not** established: why the forward reconciler did not finalise 6528 and 6549 as `sl` itself. It runs earlier in the same tick than the watchdog, with the same flat confirm. For the reconciler to lose, it must have been skipping those rows: a failed order read, a live-status read, or a raise in `_close_trade_from_order_status`, which pops its confirm and re-arms on the next tick. The logs are gone, so this cannot be settled. **This PR is what makes it decidable next time.**

### The exact change (`src/runtime/order_monitor.py`)

- `_RECONCILER_LAST_SEEN`: an in-process dict, `trades.id → short verdict`, capped at 5000 entries. `_note_reconciler_seen` writes it and never raises. `_reconciler_last_seen` reads it.
- `_reconcile_open_trades` records its verdict at every per-row skip or wait: `grace_window`, `account_no_cfg`, `account_dry`, `non_order_id`, `order_read_failed`, `order_live:<status>`, `not_found_*`, `positions_read_failed`, `symbol_unreadable`, `position_alive`, `flat_pending_confirm`, `close_write_failed:<ExcType>`.
- `_watchdog_stuck_strategies` writes `notes["reconciler_last"]` and adds `reconciler_last=` to its WARNING line, on **both** finalise branches. The recovered branch wraps this in a try, so the stamp can never block the close write.

### Why it is safe

- Nothing branches on the new state. There is no new order, gate, halt, mode flip or RiskManager change, and no exit price, PnL or exit reason changes. Re-pricing stays with PI-20261010-RNCT2YDP-0001.
- The only write is one extra short key in `trades.notes`. That goes through `dump_capped(…, 500)`, which trims the longest string first, so existing keys keep their priority.
- Memory is bounded (5000 entries × ≤60 chars), and a restart starts empty (`not_seen_this_process`).

### Revert

`git revert <merge sha>`. There is no schema change, no data migration and no config change.

### What closes the row after deploy

The next `stuck_strategy_watchdog` (or watchdog-`recovered`) finalise on any Bybit account carries `notes.reconciler_last`. That value names the reconciler branch that let the watchdog win, and it is the input to a targeted fix. If two weekly re-reads (PI-20261010-WQAPZD8B-0001, next due 2026-10-31) show **0** watchdog closes on bybit_1, bybit_2 and bybit_portfolio, the item can be closed `done` on #17455 + #18514, and this stamp stays as a detector.

## Architecture impact

- [x] **Not applicable**: bookkeeping inside the existing monitor tick. No schema, contract, API or config change.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_watchdog_reconciler_last.py` (new, 7): the reconciler records `order_read_failed`, `order_live:new` and `flat_pending_confirm`. The watchdog's unmatched and recovered finalises carry `reconciler_last`. The never-seen case reads `not_seen_this_process`. The record is bounded and never raises.
- [x] 27 adjacent watchdog / reconciler / exit-cluster / own-leg / netting suites: 538 passed.
- [x] `ruff check` (the pinned `<0.16`) on the touched files: clean.
- [x] `python3 scripts/ci/run_guards.py --base-ref main` (see the lane report for the result).
- [ ] CI green

## Filed for follow-ups

- PI-20261024-E4A4JHBS-0001: bybit_1 rows 6622 (booked `sl_cross`, but its own SL filled) and 6634 (closed by a sibling's order) carry wrong labels that no live sweep can correct. This needs a reviewed one-shot relabel, or a kill if paper history is not worth a writeback.
- PI-20261010-WQAPZD8B-0001 was re-dated with this observation.
